children: unveiled a small handheld AI device called Meta Charm at its Connect event on Wednesday, expanding its hardware push beyond smart glasses as technology companies look for new ways to bring AI beyond the smartphone.
Roughly the size of an Apple AirPods case, Charm features an approximately 2-inch OLED touchscreen and built-in 5G connectivity. Meta
said the device is expected to ship in December ahead of the holiday season but has not disclosed pricing.
Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg said Charm brings the company’s Muse personal AI agent into a portable device that can be carried on a keychain, in a pocket, or with a wrist strap.

“We pack the whole Muse experience, including the whole real-time voice and avatar stack, into something that fits on a keychain and is always available to talk to,” Zuckerberg said at Meta’s annual device event, Meta Connect, in Menlo Park, California.

The device includes speakers, microphones, front- and rear-facing cameras, a USB-C port, and a customizable virtual Muse character, including options for its appearance and voice. Charm is designed as a dedicated interface for Muse rather than a smartphone replacement.

Charm can connect to Muse over 5G when Wi-Fi is unavailable and is paired and synchronized through the Muse app on an iPhone or Android device. It also supports music and video playback but does not offer phone or video calling. Two Charm devices can also recognize and interact with each other when placed nearby.
launched Muse earlier this month as a personal AI agent that can handle tasks including sending emails, booking travel, filling out forms, and making purchases on a user’s behalf.

title: Meta unveils keychain-sized Charm gadget for Muse AI agent
